children: Australian stocks are poised to rise at the open after U.S. equities reversed course following early heavy losses. ASX futures are up by 0.7% ahead of Thursday's session, suggesting the S&P/ASX 200 will rally from a 0.4% drop that was its ninth decline in 10 sessions. The benchmark index is down by 2.4% in November amid uncertainty over whether the country's central bank has finished interest rates. Ahead of the open, gold miner Northern Star Resources said its chief operating officer had resigned. Perseus Mining said its CFO will leave in early 2027. U.S. indices were mixed, although tech stocks lost more ground. The DJIA added 0.3%, the S&P 500 fell 0.25%, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.6%. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
